title: functioncall-eval-contracts-and-onboarding-checklist-2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This guide defines a standard evaluation contract and an onboarding checklist for models that use function/tool-calling interfaces (a.k.a. functioncall or toolcall). It covers: what to measure, how to construct prompt and probe sets, quantization considerations, quality gate thresholds, and a regression triage fast-path for function-calling failure modes. Use this doc to certify a model (hosted, dedicated, or private) for production traffic that exercises the tool-calling surface.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: applied ML engineers, model infra owners, SREs, platform QA, and product engineers integrating tools.
- Scope: text-only and multimodal models that expose structured function output or tool invocation APIs. Not for purely embedding-only endpoints.

Why this matters:
Function-calling expands app capabilities but creates deterministic integration contracts (JSON schema, sequence-of-calls semantics, and failure/retry behaviors). Failures manifest as malformed JSON, wrong tool selection, missing params, or silent no-op calls — which have higher user-impact than standard free-text regressions. We need a reproducible, automated way to validate these behaviors across model variants, quantized artifacts, and rollout channels.

Evaluation contract (machine-readable):
Every model onboarding request must supply an eval contract json that declares the following fields. This schema is the minimum expected artifact attached to a model card.

Example eval_contract.json:
```
{
  "model_id": "redwood-llamax-13b-v3",
  "interface": "functioncalling-v1",
  "schemas": [
    {"name": "search_file", "json_schema": "{\\\"type\\\":\\\"object\\\",...}", "required_samples": 200},
    {"name": "summarize_page", "json_schema": "{\\\"type\\\":\\\"object\\\",...}", "required_samples": 150}
  ],
  "quant_profiles_tested": ["fp16","int8-ggml"],
  "primary_prompt_set": "/datasets/functioncall/checkout-2026-v1",
  "slo_targets": {"parse_rate": 0.995, "correct_tool_selection": 0.98, "latency_ms_p95": 800}
}
```

Key contract fields (human-readable):
- model_id: canonical model reference used in runtime routing.
- interface: cataloged interface type (functioncalling-v1, functioncalling-v2, toolchain-v1).
- schemas: list of named function/tool schemas with their canonical JSON Schema and minimum sample count for evaluation.
- quant_profiles_tested: quantization artifacts that must be validated (list).
- primary_prompt_set: pointer to the canonical probe/prompt dataset.
- slo_targets: minimal quality/latency thresholds to pass the gate.

Prompt & probe design principles:
1) Intent diversity: For each declared schema, include probes that exercise intent synonyms, misspellings, nested requests, and numeric edge cases.
2) Structural fuzzing: Include syntactic noise that commonly breaks parsers: mismatched punctuation, truncated sentences, and nested JSON in text blocks.
3) Multi-step sequences: For function chains (tool A -> tool B), model must demonstrate correct ordering under simulated session state.
4) Latency-sensitive probes: Tiny-context and long-context variants — measure p50/p95/p99 for both token-generation and post-processing (parse time).
5) Quantization sensitivity: For each probe, run on floating-point baseline and at least two quantized variants to capture divergent behavior.

Sample prompt matrix (short table represented as text):
- schema: search_file | probes: 200 | categories: exact-match, fuzzy-query, truncated-path, escaped-characters
- schema: summarize_page | probes: 150 | categories: long-context, single-sentence, list-based, nested-bullets

Automated checks (must pass to promote to canary):
- Parse success rate (parse_rate): fraction of probes returning syntactically valid JSON matching schema. Target >= slo_targets.parse_rate.
- Tool selection accuracy (correct_tool_selection): fraction of probes that select the expected function/tool. Target >= slo_targets.correct_tool_selection.
- Semantic correctness (semantic_score): automated heuristics + small human annotation sample. Thresholds depend on product (default >= 0.85 for conversational tool workflows).
- Latency SLOs: token-generate + parse <= slo_targets.latency_ms_p95.
- Determinism budget: For deterministic routes, p95 token divergence <= 1.2x baseline variance.

Quality guardrails and blocking failures:
- Blocker: Returning top-level free-text when schema required (e.g., response is plain text instead of JSON) — immediate rollback for canaries.
- Blocker: Incorrect tool invoked when expected tool has security implications (delete/write operations).
- High-severity: Missing required keys in returned JSON across >2% of probes.
- Medium-severity: Parsable but semantically incorrect params (e.g., wrong file id).

Quantization & artifact considerations:
- All quantized artifacts used in production must be part of the eval_contract.quant_profiles_tested list.
- Run the quantized-replay orchestrator (see /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/quantized-artifact-eval-gate-and-rollout-2026) with the same seed and prompt ordering to detect brittle tokenization-induced parse fractures.
- If parse_rate drops by >1% between fp16 and int8 on any schema, trigger conservative rollout (no auto-promote).

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step):
1) Prepare artifacts: model binary, tokenizer config, eval_contract.json, primary_prompt_set (as JSONL), and a human annotation plan.
2) Local smoke: run 100 probe smoke harness with both baseline and quantized artifacts.
   CLI: ```./tools/run_probe_harness --model ./bin/model.pt --prompts prompts.jsonl --out results.jsonl --mode smoke```
3) Full eval: schedule an isolated canary evaluation job on the eval-cluster with the contract. Tag run with model_id and git sha.
4) Review metrics: parse_rate, correct_tool_selection, semantic_score, latency percentiles. Attach the annotated sample.
5) Human validation: sample 200 probes for each schema with a 3-rater majority label for correctness.
6) Security review: for tool calls that touch data stores or external systems, run threat checklist and confirm RBAC/KMS integration.
7) Sign-off: model owner and platform QA MUST approve. Update model registry with signed eval_contract.json.

Canary rollout policy (recommended):
- Canary phase 1 (internal-only): 0.5% of traffic, 24 hours, realtime monitoring for parse_rate and key SLOs.
- Canary phase 2 (gradual escalation): 2.5% traffic, 48 hours with auto-rollback if parse_rate drops by >0.5% or lat_p95 increases by >25%.
- Promote to baseline after 7 days of stable metrics and negative regression on regression-scan.

Regression triage fast-path (if canary or prod shows functioncall failures):
1) Capture failing traces: include request_id, prompt snapshot, tokenizer state, model_variant, quant_profile, and runtime route.
2) Reproduce in isolation: replay using quantized-replay-orchestrator.
3) Bisect by artifact: switch between model versions, tokenizers, and quant artifacts to isolate change.
4) If parse errors only in quantized artifact, tag as QUANT_FAILURE and escalate to infra-quant team.
5) For semantic failures (wrong-tool), run probe-slice amplification to find minimal prompt that flips selection and open a regression issue.
6) Rollback criteria: sustained parse_rate drop >1% over 1 hour OR single catastrophic security-invoking miscall.

Telemetry and dashboards (what to instrument):
- parse_rate (rolling 5m / 1h), correct_tool_selection, semantic_score (approx), p50/p95/p99 latency, error classes (malformed, missing-key, wrong-tool).
- Annotated-sample drift signal: fraction of human labels disagreeing with automated heuristics.
- Quant-profile comparison chart: delta(parse_rate fp16, int8) by schema.

Ownership and escalation matrix:
- Model Owner: primary contact for onboarding, responsible for eval_contract and fixes.
- Eval Platform: owns harness infra and gating automation.
- Quant Team: owns quant artifacts and kernel selection.
- Security: owns high-severity tool-call gating.
- Oncall escalation order: Model Owner -> Eval Platform -> Quant Team -> Security (if data/store impact).

Operational recipes (quick commands):
- Run full contract locally: ```python infra/eval_runner.py --contract eval_contract.json --out results/$(date +%F)-full.json```
- Extract failing slice: ```jq -r '.probes[] | select(.status=="failed")' results.jsonl > failing_slice.jsonl```
- Compare quant artifacts: ```./tools/compare_quant --baseline fp16.bin --compare int8.bin --prompts prompts.jsonl```

Appendix A — Example failure report template (use for triage issues):
- title: [Regression][functioncall] search_file parse-rate drop on canary
- summary: brief description with model_id and canary window
- impact: delta parse_rate, affected routes, user-visible impact
- reproduction: exact commands + env + seed
- artifacts: model binary sha, tokenizer sha, quant profile id
- initial hypothesis: e.g., tokenization drift after new tokenizer mapping
- proposed mitigation: rollback, narrow-canary, or patch

Appendix B — Suggested prompt set naming and storage conventions:
- /datasets/functioncall/{team}-{intentset}-v{YYYYMM} e.g. /datasets/functioncall/search-team-checkout-v202601
- Include companion metadata.json with fields: created_by, sample_counts, schema_coverage, seed, source_revision

Appendix C — References and related playbooks:
- evaluator-interchange-format-and-federation-spec-2026 (interop format for evaluators)
- quantized-artifact-eval-gate-and-rollout-2026 (quant gate and safety thresholds)
- eval-oncall-runbook-for-model-regression-debugging-2026 (oncall playbook)
